1: Details & Features
The modular storage system is the ideal addition to compressor systems and ensures a stable pressure supply for air and gas applications. Available in pressure stages of 330 bar and 420 bar, it reduces pressure fluctuations during peak demand and reduces the frequency of compressor start-ups. Flexible expansion with 50- or 80-litre storage cylinders allows the system to be tailored precisely to requirements and supports smooth, efficient system operation.: Storage cylinder with console
A module consists of a storage cylinder that is pre-piped and ready for connection, mounted on a console for floor or wall installation. Based on 50 l or 80 l storage cylinders, these storage systems can be expanded as required.: Pressure vessel
The storage cylinders comply with DGRL2014/68/EU (PED) and are intended for stationary applications.: Condensate drain
Depending on the application or due to insufficient air or gas treatment, condensate can accumulate in high-pressure storage systems. All standard storage vessels from BAUER KOMPRESSOREN are therefore equipped with a manual condensate drain.: Options
Safety valve and pressure gauge: Safety valve and pressure gauge are mounted on the console of the first module. This is mandatory if exceeding the maximum permissible storage pressure cannot be otherwise avoided, e.g. by approved safety valves on the compressor or in the pipeline.
The storage design: Storage system design – the basis for efficient compressor operation
A correctly dimensioned storage system is one of the key components of a high-pressure setup. It reduces pressure fluctuations during intermittent air withdrawal and decreases compressor start frequency by providing sufficient storage capacity. The pressure vessels and final separators in high-pressure compressors are designed for a limited number of load cycles. Fewer start-stop cycles significantly extend the service life of these components.: To ensure optimal operation, the compressor should ideally run no more than two to four cycles per hour. BAUER industrial compressors are equipped with cycle counters as standard, which record actual start cycles and support safe, efficient system control.
The size of the storage system depends on:: Compressor delivery rate (l/min)
Air consumption of the specific application: Pressure differential between start and stop (hysteresis)
Simplified formula for sizing a high-pressure storage system (based on 4 load cycles/hour):: Vk (l/min): Compressor delivery volume in liters per minute
V (l): Storage volume in liters (water volume): Δp (bar): Pressure differential (hysteresis) in bar
We recommend a pressure differential Δp of max. 60 bar for continuous operation. Within this range, stationary high-pressure storage cylinders are typically rated for continuous duty. For higher differentials, the number of allowable filling cycles is limited. Please refer to the documentation for the specific pressure vessel.: Downloads

What
pressure ranges does the GIB 23 series cover?
Depending on the configuration and available inlet pressure, GIB 23 high-pressure booster compressors achieve final pressures of approximately 90 to 420 bar.
What
flow rates do the GIB 23 boosters provide?
The GIB 23 series covers flow rates of approximately 1,450 to 3,900 litres per minute. The actual flow rate depends on the inlet pressure, final pressure and system configuration.
Which
gases can be compressed with GIB 23 boosters?
GIB 23 boosters are designed for the compression of Air, Nitrogen, Helium, Heliox and Argon. They are specifically developed for industrial applications with increased pressure requirements.
How
are GIB 23 boosters controlled and monitored?
The boosters are equipped with the B-CONTROL MICRO control system. It enables easy operation, reliable monitoring of all relevant operating parameters and connection to the B-CLOUD and the B-APP for digital system monitoring.
What
advantages does the B-CLOUD offer for GIB 23 booster applications?
The B-CLOUD enables digital remote monitoring of the booster system. Operating data, alarms and system statuses can be accessed in real time, supporting predictive maintenance and high system availability.

ation and increases the operational safety of the compressor system by providing early information about critical fill levels.
Connection for external air inlet
When filling breathing air cylinders, the quality of the compressed air depends on the quality of the ambient air being drawn in. Particularly when exhaust gases (CO) or ventilation from other equipment may enter the compressor room, pure fresh air must be drawn in from outside. For this purpose, a connection for an external air inlet is provided.
B-CONTROL III
The B-CONTROL III is the premium control system for complex applications. Its 7-inch touchscreen display provides a user-friendly visualization of all operating data. Features such as a data logger, USB interface, Remote HMI, and protocols including OPC UA, Modbus, and CAN bus are integrated. The control system supports up to four compressors in a network and can be expanded flexibly.
Particle filter
An integrated particle filter is optionally available in combination with the P 41, P 61, and P 81 purification systems, ensuring consistently high purity levels.
Intermediate pressure gauge
Analog pressure gauges are installed at appropriate points of the compressor system and allow for easy monitoring of operating pressures. They support diagnostics and simplify maintenance work on the system.

A correctly dimensioned storage system is one of the key components of a high-pressure setup. It reduces pressure fluctuations during intermittent air withdrawal and decreases compressor start frequency by providing sufficient storage capacity. The pressure vessels and final separators in high-pressure compressors are designed for a limited number of load cycles. Fewer start-stop cycles significantly extend the service life of these components.: To ensure optimal operation, the compressor should ideally run no more than two to four cycles per hour. BAUER industrial compressors are equipped with cycle counters as standard, which record actual start cycles and support safe, efficient system control.

What
pressure ranges does the GIB 23 series cover?
Depending on the configuration and available inlet pressure, GIB 23 high-pressure booster compressors achieve final pressures of approximately 90 to 420 bar.
What
flow rates do the GIB 23 boosters provide?
The GIB 23 series covers flow rates of approximately 1,450 to 3,900 litres per minute. The actual flow rate depends on the inlet pressure, final pressure and system configuration.
Which
gases can be compressed with GIB 23 boosters?
GIB 23 boosters are designed for the compression of Air, Nitrogen, Helium, Heliox and Argon. They are specifically developed for industrial applications with increased pressure requirements.
How
are GIB 23 boosters controlled and monitored?
The boosters are equipped with the B-CONTROL MICRO control system. It enables easy operation, reliable monitoring of all relevant operating parameters and connection to the B-CLOUD and the B-APP for digital system monitoring.
What
advantages does the B-CLOUD offer for GIB 23 booster applications?
The B-CLOUD enables digital remote monitoring of the booster system. Operating data, alarms and system statuses can be accessed in real time, supporting predictive maintenance and high system availability.

Connection for external air inlet
When filling breathing air cylinders, the quality of the compressed air depends on the quality of the ambient air being drawn in. Particularly when exhaust gases (CO) or ventilation from other equipment may enter the compressor room, pure fresh air must be drawn in from outside. For this purpose, a connection for an external air inlet is provided.
B-CONTROL III
The B-CONTROL III is the premium control system for complex applications. Its 7-inch touchscreen display provides a user-friendly visualization of all operating data. Features such as a data logger, USB interface, Remote HMI, and protocols including OPC UA, Modbus, and CAN bus are integrated. The control system supports up to four compressors in a network and can be expanded flexibly.
Particle filter
An integrated particle filter is optionally available in combination with the P 41, P 61, and P 81 purification systems, ensuring consistently high purity levels.
Intermediate pressure gauge
Analog pressure gauges are installed at appropriate points of the compressor system and allow for easy monitoring of operating pressures. They support diagnostics and simplify maintenance work on the system.
